transcript: Your team presents the same onboarding deck to every new starter. What if they could watch it on day one, at their own pace, with the same message every time?
Start by sorting your decks into three groups. Stable policies and company history suit video, things that change often stay out, and welcomes and Q&A stay live.
A new hire is more likely to finish five six-minute videos than one thirty-minute video. So split your content into short, focused topics.
Tidy each deck first. Give every slide one idea and a headline that makes a point, and swap stale names for roles like your manager.
Your speaker notes become the voiceover, so write them like you're explaining things to a new colleague. Keep sentences short and spell out acronyms.
When a policy changes, just edit the slide and convert again. On Pro, a.i. directs each video so it lands like a produced welcome. Try Basic first at powerpoint2vid.com.
